name: \(\phi_B = B A \cos \theta\)
content: Magnetic flux when the magnetic field is at an angle \(\theta\) to the surface normal
e: Magnetic flux when the magnetic field is at an angle θ to the surface normal is written φB = B A cos θ. Flux is B A cosθ; full when B is perpendicular to the area and zero when B lies in the plane.

name: \(\phi_B = B A\)
content: Magnetic flux when the field is perpendicular to the surface area (\(\theta = 0^\circ\))
e: Magnetic flux when the field is perpendicular to the surface area (θ = 0^°) is written φB = B A. Flux is B A cosθ; full when B is perpendicular to the area and zero when B lies in the plane.

name: \(\phi_B = 0\)
content: Magnetic flux when the field is parallel to the surface area (\(\theta = 90^\circ\))
e: Magnetic flux when the field is parallel to the surface area (θ = 90^°) is written φB = 0. In parallel, the same voltage sits across each branch and the currents add. Flux is B A cosθ; full when B is perpendicular to the area and zero when B lies in the plane.

name: \(E = -\frac{d\phi_B}{dt}\)
content: Faraday's Law of induction for a single turn wire loop
e: Faraday's Law of induction for a single turn wire loop is written E = -(dφB)/(dt). Faraday's law: induced emf equals the rate of change of magnetic flux through the loop. One farad is one coulomb per volt, so practical capacitors are µF, nF or pF.

name: \(E = -N \frac{d\phi_B}{dt}\)
content: Faraday's Law of induction for a wire loop with \(N\) identical turns
e: Faraday's Law of induction for a wire loop with N identical turns is written E = -N (dφB)/(dt). One farad is one coulomb per volt, so practical capacitors are µF, nF or pF. Faraday's law: induced emf equals the rate of change of magnetic flux through the loop.

name: \(P = VI\)
content: Electrical power formula in terms of voltage and current
e: Electrical power formula in terms of voltage and current is written P = VI. Current is charge passing a point each second, and it needs a closed path. Electrical power is the energy transfer rate, P = VI, also I^2R or V^2/R.

name: \(I = \frac{P}{V}\)
e: Current calculation for power transmission is written I = (P)/(V). Current is charge passing a point each second, and it needs a closed path.

name: \(B = \mu H\)
content: Relationship between magnetic flux density and magnetic field strength
e: Relationship between magnetic flux density and magnetic field strength is written B = µ H. Flux is B A cosθ; full when B is perpendicular to the area and zero when B lies in the plane. Flux density B is magnetic lines through unit area perpendicular to the field.

name: \(\phi_B = \int \vec{B} \cdot d\vec{A}\)
e: Definition of magnetic flux integral is written φB = integral B · dA. Flux is B A cosθ; full when B is perpendicular to the area and zero when B lies in the plane.

name: \(E = E_m \sin \omega t\)
e: Alternating electromotive force (emf) is written E = Em sin ω t. Emf is energy per coulomb that a source pumps around a complete loop.

name: \(I = I_m \sin \omega t\)
e: Alternating current is written I = Im sin ω t. Current is charge passing a point each second, and it needs a closed path. AC reverses on a clock; household supply is this reversing current.

name: \(E = N B A \omega \sin \omega t\)
content: Induced emf generated in an AC generator
e: Induced emf generated in an AC generator is written E = N B A ω sin ω t. A changing magnetic flux through a loop produces an induced emf and, if the path is closed, an induced current. AC reverses on a clock; household supply is this reversing current.

name: \(\frac{V_s}{V_p} = \frac{E_s}{E_p} = \frac{N_s}{N_p} = \frac{I_p}{I_s}\)
content: Transformer relationship between voltage, emf, turns ratio, and current
e: Transformer relationship between voltage, emf, turns ratio, and current is written (Vs)/(Vp) = (Es)/(Ep) = (Ns)/(Np) = (Ip)/(Is). Voltage is potential difference, energy per unit charge between two points. Current is charge passing a point each second, and it needs a closed path.
